Delicious Library, 2004

A Mac cataloguing app that showed books, films, and games as photoreal covers on a wooden bookshelf.

Source
Wikipedia: Delicious Monster
Creator
Delicious Monster (Wil Shipley and Mike Matas)
Made
First released November 2004; Delicious Library 2 in 2008
Style
Skeuomorphism (precursor; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Warm, collectible, crafted
Evidence
The archived 2009 website (capture) shows a small screenshot of the shelves, too small to describe. Based on Wikipedia and TechCrunch (2010).
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Delicious Monster was founded by Wil Shipley and Mike Matas; Matas left in 2005 to work for Apple. Delicious Library won Apple Design Awards, including Best Mac OS X User Experience (2005). Wikipedia: Delicious Monster.

The software was first released in November 2004; Delicious Library 2 was released in 2008. Wikipedia: Delicious Library.

TechCrunch (27 January 2010): “the bookshelf view in iBooks is nearly identical to the main bookshelf view used in Delicious Library.” TechCrunch.

Why it belongs

The link from this app to iBooks through one designer shows how the style moved from independent Mac software into Apple’s own apps.
